To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
model-guided empirical optimizations can be used to generate SIMD code for multimedia extension architectures.
model-guided empirical compiler optimization can be used to achieve performance that is competitive to state-of-the-art libraries.

(a) model-guided empirical compiler optimization can be applied to a wide range of problems, (b) model-guided optimization can be used in combination with automatic code generation, and (c) model-guided compilation of multimedia extensions can be applied to large problems, including matrix multiply, and outperform the best hand-coded libraries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to effectively utilize the memory hierarchy and SIMD compute engines in multimedia extensions.
the design, implementation and evaluation of a model-guided, empirical compiler that automatically generates efficient code for multimedia extensions.
developing compiler technology to enable effective use of the memory hierarchy for multimedia extensions, and to automatically generate SIMD code for multimedia extension architectures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have demonstrated a new approach to the problem of multimedia extension compiler optimization that can produce code that is competitive with hand-tuned libraries and can be used to produce code that is within 10% of the best performing library for a wide variety of workloads and architectures.
we have demonstrated that a single compiler can achieve the performance levels that previously required a hand-tuned library and a compiler that is hand-tuned for specific architectures.
our compiler is the first to demonstrate the feasibility of a model-guided, self-tuning, superword-level parallelizing compiler for multimedia extensions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our compiler is able to generate SIMD code for multimedia instructions with performance that is competitive with the state-of-the-art libraries, and does so with minimal user interaction.
we have achieved a compiler that can produce code that is competitive with state-of-the-art libraries and that is within 10% of hand-tuned assembly code.
we have successfully combined model-guided empirical compilation for memory hierarchy optimizations with a backend compiler that exploits superword parallelism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
model-guided empirical optimizations can be used to effectively optimize for all levels in the memory hierarchy.
a compiler that combines model-guided empirical optimizations and SIMD code generation can be a viable alternative to self-tuning libraries and hand-tuned code for multimedia extensions.
model-guided empirical optimizations can be used effectively to tune multimedia extensions, and that this can be done without requiring any hand-tuned SIMD kernels.
